title: Optimal Lipschitz Balancing Weights at the Critical Radius: A Marked Poisson Limit
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4; NOT salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope.
paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived stationary Poisson attainment, dependent-load boundary repair, finite-block risk brackets, and the strict interior frontier for a one-dimensional uniform fair-randomization design. D0.5 graded the delivered package subfield: it lacks quantitative certificate rates, executed frontier values, and a broader design or application, so it cannot meet the required field floor within this anchor. The panel also left a coefficient-sign reconciliation and theorem-level related-work comparison unresolved; a spatial-frontier extension would require a distinct re-anchor, and no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: At the critical analyst radius \(C_n=c\sqrt n\), the published Armstrong--Kolesar full affine RMSE optimizer has the same sign-constrained matching-multiplier form as the transport optimizer, and its normalized variance and Wasserstein coordinates converge to the unique coordinates \((v(c),b(c))\) of an attained stationary Bernoulli-marked Poisson program. Every finite \(c>0\) lies strictly away from nearest-neighbor matching: \(b(c)>1\) and \(v(c)<11/2\), so the thermodynamic frontier has no finite matching elbow even though each finite design eventually does. Free and closed renewal-block convex programs give computable certified risk enclosures, and concave difference quotients give certified enclosures for both coordinates. Conditional Gaussian inference for the smaller true unit-Lipschitz class is a corollary; generic growing-radius bias-aware inference is due to Armstrong--Kolesar.
gap: Finite-design minimax Lipschitz weights and generic growing-radius inference are known, but the literature neither selects the critical sequence \(C_n=c\sqrt n\) nor characterizes its exact stochastic risk and coordinates; existing stationary random-measure transport fixes destination masses, and stabilization laws do not cover globally optimized loads.
fill: The project derives the critical scaling from the exact finite identity, formulates the limiting optimization under a stationary law with a separate point-Palm evaluation, proves finite-to-stationary convergence of the optimizer coordinates, constructs certified fresh-variable finite-block brackets, resolves the strict interior endpoint curve, and transfers the variance limit to conditional Gaussian coverage.
